jane_cust: Hey team — since ~02:10 UTC we're getting sporadic 5xx + high tail latency from our integration. We see requests from our on‑prem VPC being routed to eu-central (huge RTT) instead of us-west. Example: req_ABC123. Auth sometimes 401, sometimes OK. Billing egress jumped too. Can we triage?

maria_support: Sorry you're hitting this — we'll help. Can you paste a minimal curl with headers and the public egress IP you see from your side? Also any recent network changes (SD‑WAN failover, proxy config)?

jane_cust: Minimal repro below. No infra changes on our side except an SD‑WAN failover ~01:50 UTC to the backup path.
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}'
```
Response samples: some requests complete with ~380ms, others >1200ms and a few 502/401. Our observed egress IP: 18.200.45.71 (this is from a NAT/proxy chain).

devon_net: Thanks — can you run a traceroute to api.redwood.example and capture TLS SNI and the source IP as seen by the backend? Also paste the NAT gateway/egress appliance IDs. From your egress IP it looks like traffic is leaving via an EU‑peered NAT. That could explain region selection.

jane_cust: Traceroute and a quick tcpdump snippet attached below (snipped for brevity):
```
traceroute to api.redwood.example (34.216.10.5), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.8.0.1  0.5 ms  0.4 ms  0.4 ms
 2  198.51.100.2  5.3 ms  5.1 ms  5.0 ms
 3  52.94.213.10  45.8 ms  46.2 ms  45.9 ms
 4  18.200.45.71  360.1 ms  359.7 ms  360.3 ms
 5  34.216.10.5  380.4 ms  379.8 ms  380.0 ms
```
And tcpdump showing TLS ClientHello SNI preserved as api.redwood.example but source IP on wire is 18.200.45.71.

ash_engineering: Quick note on routing: Redwood's smart‑routing chooses region based on the *source IP* + route table that maps egress CIDRs to preferred regions. If your onprem/proxy SNATs to an EU NAT (18.200.45.0/24 in our mapping), requests will be routed to eu variants. Also some proxies rewrite X‑Forwarded‑For and we don't trust header hints for region selection if the source IP maps to a different region.

maria_support: Two immediate mitigations: 1) On our side we can enable account‑level "region_affinity": "us‑west" (temporary) to force serving from us‑west endpoints. 2) On your side, preserve source IP through the path (disable SNAT at proxy or use a US egress NAT). Which do you prefer?

jane_cust: We need a long‑term fix — disabling SNAT may be hard on the appliance vendor. Can you confirm the exact CIDR mapping you're using so we can route/whitelist correctly? Also worried about the unexpected egress billing — any way to avoid extra cross‑region egress charges while we fix?

devon_net: CIDR mapping we use (simplified):
- 34.216.0.0/16 -> us‑west
- 54.240.0.0/12 -> us‑west
- 18.194.0.0/15 -> eu‑central
- 18.200.45.0/24 -> eu‑peered (this is the IP you posted)
If your proxy SNATs to 18.200.45.71 then our routing picks eu. For billing: cross‑region egress will be billed as normal; to avoid that you need to egress from a US NAT or set our region_affinity.

ash_engineering: Repro steps we recommend so we can validate:
1) From a test host behind your proxy run `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example:443:34.216.10.5 https://api.redwood.example/` and capture the `:authority`/SNI and source IP seen by backend.
2) Run `tcpdump -ni any 'tcp port 443 and (host 34.216.10.5 or host 18.200.45.71)' -w /tmp/redwood.pcap` while repeating the request.
3) Share the pcap (redact keys) and the traceroute output.

kevin_oncall: I'll open an internal infra ticket to add a temporary account lock for region_affinity and notify billing. INC-2026-2457 created and linked. :eyes:

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-2457 created by kevin_oncall — severity P2 — routing misroute noticed. Linked resources: https://infra.redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-2457

jane_cust: Did the tests above. We can try region_affinity for now to stop the bleeding. We'll also engage our appliance vendor to stop SNAT to the EU NAT.

maria_support: Confirmed we've enabled `region_affinity: us-west` on the account as a temporary mitigation. Please test and post timings.

jane_cust: After the switch, latency dropped to ~40ms and auth errors disappeared for the test calls. Thanks — we'll roll out a config change to the proxy to preserve source IP and add a static route to use the US egress path.

devon_net: Root cause summary for the ticket: on‑prem SD‑WAN failover caused proxy appliances to pick a path that SNATted outbound traffic to a peered EU NAT. Redwood's region selection uses source IP mapping which incorrectly sent traffic to EU endpoints. Fix = preserve source IP or ensure US NAT path; we also recommend customers set an explicit region_affinity for short windows.

jane_cust: Great, will validate fully tomorrow and close the incident once stable. Thanks for the quick help everyone. :pray:
__notes: thread follows agents.md: single string with chronological messages, no title field
